NVDA.rationale: Nvidia exhibits exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +43% QoQ), EPS of $2.39 (+215% YoY), gross margin of 74.9%, operating margin of 65.6%, net margin of 71.4%, and operating cash flow of $50.3B in a single quarter. The balance sheet is fortress-like with $195.5B equity against only $8.47B debt (debt-to-equity 0.043). Data center revenue of $75.2B grew 92% YoY, and Q2 guidance of $91B signals continued acceleration. The company holds ~87% of merchant AI data center revenue and 90% of discrete GPU shipments. However, the TTM data is incomplete (fiscal quarter gap), so I cannot confirm trailing twelve-month trends with full confidence. Valuation is attractive vs. own history: the current P/E of 29.8 sits at the very bottom of its 365-day range (29.0-66.8), and P/B of 24.3 is similarly at the low end (23.7-57.8). Multiple news sources cite forward P/E of 23x, described as the lowest since 2019. This is a significant compression from the 50-57x range that prevailed through most of the past year, despite earnings power that has roughly doubled. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 FY2027 earnings report on August 26, with consensus EPS of ~$2.08 and revenue guidance of $91B. Hyperscaler capex guidance has been raised (Alphabet to $195-205B, TSMC to $60-64B), and Vera Rubin production has been confirmed by Jensen Huang. Risks include China export restrictions (China revenue excluded from guidance), potential circular financing concerns with OpenAI, and rising interest rates (10Y at 4.68%). Michael Burry is short, and the stock has underperformed YTD (+11% vs S&P +8%). News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.424). The score of +0.45 reflects excellent fundamentals and cheap valuation vs. history, tempered by the incomplete TTM picture, macro headwinds (rising rates, inflation), and China regulatory risk that prevents a full +0.5.
